floor_history.headline: MoveImage floor 21 -> 7 and build_insns 47 -> 49 (== target): hoisting `D_8009BF28 = packed;` to be the first primitive store puts `sll $v0,$s1,16` at the head of the post-guard block, so reorg's eage

MoveImage floor 7 -> 2 (build_insns 49 == target): walking the rect argument with a post-increment pointer hoists the rect[0] read ahead of the D_8009BF28 store WITHOUT losing the H2 delay-slot steal;

frontier.hypothesis: H7 - the entire residual is one scheduler pick at T-5 (insn 80, the D_8009BF2C store, prio 3, beats insn 91, the p[6] load, prio 2). Target's build must have priority(91) >= priority(80), and since the rank_for_schedule class tie-break already favours 91 at T-5 (91 is independent of the last-scheduled insn 86, whereas 86 depends on 80), a lift of exactly +1 on 91 is sufficient - it does not have to exceed 80.
frontier.mechanism: cc1 2.7.2 sched.c priority() = longest TRUE-dependence path from the block start; anti/output links cost 0. priority(91) = priority(83) + 1 and the dev-table load 83 is depth 1 because cc1 disambiguates %lo(D_8009BE6C) from every store in the block (the two symbol stores, and the `0x0($a1)` store whose base carries a REG_EQUIV to &D_8009BF24). Any source structure that puts ONE true-dependence edge into the dev-table load closes the function.
frontier.next_probe: FORENSICS modality. Dump `.sched`/`.sched2` for the MATCHED siblings in the same TU that use the identical dev-table dispatch (LoadImage, StoreImage, ClearImage, ClearImage2 - src/display.c:129-163) and read the priority of each one's `p[N]` argument load relative to its neighbouring stores. If any matched sibling shows its dev-table load at depth >= 2, whatever produces that depth in the sibling is the missing structure here, and it is ground truth rather than a guess. Reuse tmp/grind/MoveImage/s2/dump.sh (it already reproduces the sandbox's exact cc1 invocation with -dr -dS -dR -dj).

frontier.hypothesis: The +1 that H7 needs may come from the guard region rather than the body: the two `lh` guard loads and the func_8007B3A8 call sit in earlier blocks, and the dev-table load's depth is measured WITHIN block 3 only. If the dev-table read were expressed so that it is fed by a value produced in the body (rather than being a self-contained lui/lw pair with no predecessor), 83 becomes depth >= 2 and 91 becomes 3.
frontier.mechanism: priority() is computed per basic block from LOG_LINKS, so an insn with no in-block predecessor is depth 1 by definition. The dev-table load currently has none. A true (not anti, which costs 0) in-block predecessor - a register dependence on a value computed in the body, or a memory dependence cc1 cannot disambiguate - lifts it.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate honest C shapes in which the dev-table pointer is REACHED THROUGH something already computed in the body, and check each for (a) build_insns == 49 and (b) whether the emitted dev-table load still uses the bare `lui $v1,%hi / lw $v1,%lo` pair target has. Any shape that survives both is a candidate. Note the anti-cheat boundary explicitly: a dependence manufactured by a construct with no semantic purpose (a dead store, an opaque holder, a volatile coercion) is a cheat, not a lever - the edge has to come from a computation the function genuinely performs.

frontier.hypothesis: The remaining search space is narrow, fully characterised, and gated by a cheap mechanical test, which makes it a good fit for a directed permuter campaign rather than more hand enumeration.
frontier.mechanism: The target is a single known edge in cc1's dependence graph and the acceptance test is two numbers from one sandbox run (score 0 with build_insns == 49). The structural axis has now been swept ~50 forms deep by hand with no movement, so random/directed mutation over the body is the cheaper remaining search.
frontier.next_probe: PERMUTER modality with a clean single-function target built from asm/funcs/MoveImage.s + tools/decomp-permuter/prelude.inc (so the function sits at offset 0 and the base score is the real weighted diff), seeded from the floor-2 candidate, with PERM_* directives over the body statement order and the dev-table access shape. Per permuter-fresh-seed-discipline, run fresh-seed windows and harvest in-turn; every closing form is a PROPOSAL and must clear the 6-test cheat checklist plus the layer-1 reviewer before it can be submitted.
